item.content:encoded:
A journey shaped by resilience, compassion and a commitment to serving others takes centre stage on this week's fijivillage Her-Story with Temalesi Vono, as Minister for Women, Children and Social Protection Sashi Kiran shares the experiences that have defined her life.

Kiran reflects on the lessons that shaped her values, and she opens up about issues close to her heart, including violence against women and children, drugs, HIV, peacebuilding, and the importance of creating opportunities for vulnerable communities.

item.title: Two taxi drivers badly assaulted in separate Wainibokasi attacks
item.description: Two taxi drivers were badly assaulted in separate incidents in Wainibokasi this month, with one driver also allegedly being robbed and having his taxi stolen. Mahen Datt, who operates from the Gulam Nabi Street taxi base in Nausori, is recovering after he was attacked, robbed and had his taxi stolen during a trip to Wainibokasi last Tuesday evening.
item.content:encoded:
Two taxi drivers were badly assaulted in separate incidents in Wainibokasi this month, with one driver also allegedly being robbed and having his taxi stolen.

Mahen Datt, who operates from the Gulam Nabi Street taxi base in Nausori, is recovering after he was attacked, robbed and had his taxi stolen during a trip to Wainibokasi last Tuesday evening.

Datt is calling for action to be taken against the suspect.

He told fijivillage News that he picked up a man at around 5.45pm who asked to be taken to a piggery farm in Wainibokasi.

Datt says while they were returning, the passenger, who was seated behind him, pulled out a dagger, threatened to slit his throat and demanded his money.

He claims the suspect stole about $120 in cash, his watch, a wallet containing about $50 in float and his ID cards.

Datt says he suffered a deep cut to his neck while trying to defend himself before managing to escape from the taxi.

He alleges the suspect then drove off with the taxi.

The injured driver was taken to Wainibokasi Hospital, where he was admitted for treatment.

Datt has also claimed that the same suspect allegedly attacked his cousin, Daya Nand, in a similar incident on the 18th of this month.

Nand says he is worried that this is becoming a normal occurrence.

He says he is thankful to God that nothing happened to him, as he has a family to take care of.

Police say both complaints are under investigation and officers are trying to identify the people involved.

item.title: Bua farmer calls for Police action after losing thousands of dollars to yaqona theft
item.description: A concerned farmer in Bua is calling on the Fiji Police Force to take stronger action against yaqona theft after losing thousands of dollars over the years. Iosefo Lawakeli, a registered nurse with the Ministry of Health and has a farm in Vunilagi, says repeated thefts have severely affected his livelihood.
item.content:encoded:
A concerned farmer in Bua is calling on the Fiji Police Force to take stronger action against yaqona theft after losing thousands of dollars over the years.

Iosefo Lawakeli, a registered nurse with the Ministry of Health and has a farm in Vunilagi, says repeated thefts have severely affected his livelihood.

He says he has lost a significant amount of yaqona and feels powerless to stop the ongoing theft on his farm.

Lawakeli told fijivillage News that yaqona theft has become a trend in the province over the years, and the ongoing problem is on the rise once again.

The farmer says he takes his car to the farm, which is about 2 hours walk from the village, and is planning to farm closer to the village to monitor his farm.

He says farm owners have to be in the farm to look after their produce before it is harvested.

Lawakeli says trusting village members to look after the farm is becoming difficult nowadays.

He hopes police intervention will curb the ongoing problem.

We have sent questions to police. They are yet to respond.

item.title: Construction contracts for four major bridge projects to be signed soon - Ro Filipe
item.description: Designs for 11 critical bridges have been completed, with construction contracts for four major bridge projects expected to be signed within two months as Fiji moves ahead with its infrastructure upgrade plans. Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport, Ro Filipe Tuisawau says the Critical Bridges Resilience Programme is a major focus under the Government's infrastructure pr
item.content:encoded:
Designs for 11 critical bridges have been completed, with construction contracts for four major bridge projects expected to be signed within two months as Fiji moves ahead with its infrastructure upgrade plans.

Minister for Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport, Ro Filipe Tuisawau says the Critical Bridges Resilience Programme is a major focus under the Government's infrastructure programme, aimed at improving connectivity, strengthening transport links and enhancing the quality of life for Fijians.

Ro Filipe says the detailed designs for the 11 critical bridges were completed under the Transport Infrastructure Investment Sector Project through the Asian Development Bank, with the tender process expected to be announced soon.

He says construction contracts for four critical bridges at Lami, Medrekutu, Sabeto and Lomaloma, funded by the ADB and World Bank, will be signed within two months.

The Minister says design work is also progressing for six other critical bridges, including Sawani Bridge, Namotomoto Bridge, Labasa Bridge, Nadi River Bridge, Renwick Bridge and Lomolomo Bridge, with designs expected to be finalised by the end of August before moving to the tender process.

He says bridge renewal works are also underway, including five bridges in Taveuni, with four currently in progress and the new Nalele Bridge, as well as the Tamavua-i-Wai Bridge project under JICA funding.

Ro Filipe says modular steel bridge supply and installation for six bridges is also moving forward, with tenders currently underway.

He says the bridges include Koronivia, Savu 5 and Gatward Bridge in the Central Division, and Nararavou, Maururu and Waimari Bridge in the Western Division, with work expected to begin later this year.

The Minister says the Government is also progressing with rural road upgrades under the New Capital Project, with 25 kilometres of access roads planned to support the movement of people, goods and services in rural areas.

He says these include the $14 million Rewa Vutia Road and Bridge construction project and the $2 million Nasauvakarua Access Road in Navosa.

Ro Filipe says these projects are in addition to major road, water, energy and other infrastructure developments included in the Ministry's 2026-2027 National Budget approved by Parliament.

item.title: LTA and Fiji Motorcyclists Association strengthen road safety awareness
item.description: The sessions, held at the LTA Valelevu and Lautoka offices, brought together members of the motorcycle community to discuss responsible road use, safety practices and the importance of complying with road regulations. The engagement also provided a platform for riders to share challenges they face on the roads and provide suggestions directly to the LTA.
item.content:encoded:
The sessions, held at the LTA Valelevu and Lautoka offices, brought together members of the motorcycle community to discuss responsible road use, safety practices and the importance of complying with road regulations.

The engagement also provided a platform for riders to share challenges they face on the roads and provide suggestions directly to the LTA.

The LTA says working closely with rider groups and key stakeholders is important in improving motorcycle safety and promoting better understanding between authorities and road users.

The Authority says the initiative is part of its continued efforts to create safer roads for all motorists, including motorcycle riders.

item.content:encoded:
A concerned citizen is calling on authorities to remove a wrecked vehicle that has been left blocking a lane after Nabua Bus Stop and before the Shalimar Junction, raising safety concerns for motorists and pedestrians.

The citizen says the vehicle, which was involved in an accident on Friday, has remained at the site for four days and is creating a dangerous situation, especially for drivers travelling at night.

He says the damaged vehicle is blocking an entire lane and there are no warning cones or signs around the area to alert motorists, making it difficult for drivers to navigate safely.

The citizen says the situation could lead to another accident and may also contribute to traffic congestion along the busy route.

He is urging the relevant authorities to take action and remove the vehicle from the roadside as soon as possible.

The public is also being reminded to remain alert and drive carefully when using the route, particularly at night.

Meanwhile, questions have been sent to Police.
